# Wednesday 24 June 2026

## Reverse causation in the Northvale lead-time analysis

The [[northvale-analysis-meeting-2026-06-24|Northvale analysis meeting]] settled how the [[lead-time-analysis|Lead-Time Analysis]] handles cases diagnosed soon after blood draw. The main model excludes the first year after blood draw, and every time-to-diagnosis window is reported separately in the main table. The 6-month exclusion and the no-exclusion model are named sensitivity analyses. The reasoning is in [[how-do-we-handle-reverse-causation-in-the-northvale-lead-time-analysis|How do we handle reverse causation in the Northvale lead-time analysis?]] and the general idea in [[reverse-causation-in-prediagnostic-studies|Reverse causation in prediagnostic studies]].

Mei-Lin disagreed and still prefers a 6-month exclusion: pancreatic cancer moves fast and the windows already show the gradient. Maja's case for one year was that the headline should be the estimate least contaminated by undiagnosed disease. Dmitri's MRD experience, tumour fraction rising steeply in the months before recurrence, supported her. My view: the windows are the real finding, so the single headline number should be conservative. The dissent is recorded and will appear in the paper.

Minutes of the [[halo-annual-meeting-2026|Halo Annual Meeting]] went out today. Our policy gap on multilateral data transfer is now formally on the record with the consortium.
